chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If a man rents a house for ten dirhams, lives in one room of it, and rents out another room of it for ten dirhams, there is no harm in that. He should not rent it out for more than what he rented it for, unless he makes an improvement in it.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for subletting a rented property in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of subletting (ta'jir) within the framework of Ijarah, establishing that the tenant may sublet a portion for the same rent or a higher price if they have made improvements (tahdid) that add value. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the right to derive benefit extends to the tenant, provided the core contractual terms are not violated or the property's condition is enhanced. This ruling is foundational in Usul al-Fiqh for distinguishing between simple subletting and value-added leasing.
